lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: reflection, risks, and backup plans

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic reflection, risks, and backup plans task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Drawing on their operations map, weekly grid, household and food contribution, and transportation plan from earlier this unit, the learner writes and then presents out loud to a trusted adult what worked during the capstone week, what didn't, and a specific backup plan for a risk that could come up again, and the adult confirms the presentation happened and asked at least one follow-up question.
safetyNotes: This lesson never requires an audio or video recording of the presentation; a live presentation or the written, guardian-initialed script both count as complete.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the presentation by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If presenting out loud is not possible, the learner instead writes the complete presentation as a script, covering the same three parts (what worked, what didn't, and the backup plan), and a trusted adult reads the full script and initials it to confirm they read and understood it.

materials: learner-local: paper or a document for the presentation notes or script
learner-local: the learner's completed artifacts from Lessons 1 through 5 of this unit

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Of the five systems (planning, household, food, transportation, communication), which one do you most want to strengthen going forward, and what is your first specific step?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Presentation content and specificity: Presentation names one specific thing that worked, one specific thing that didn't, and one specific backup plan naming the trigger and the different action. | Guardian-confirmed presentation and engagement: Guardian confirms the presentation happened, live or via the initialed script, and confirms asking at least one follow-up question. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a second backup plan for a different risk from a different system (for example, food or transportation) and present it using the same structure.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic reflection, risks, and backup plans task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: reflection, risks, and backup plans action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for reflection, risks, and backup plans.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: reflection, risks, and backup plans coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Drawing on their operations map, weekly grid, household and food contribution, and transportation plan from earlier this unit, the learner writes and then presents out loud to a trusted adult what worked during the capstone week, what didn't, and a specific backup plan for a risk that could come up again, and the adult confirms the presentation happened and asked at least one follow-up question.
Coach direction: Review your artifacts from earlier in the capstone week and outline what worked and what didn't across the systems you used.
Learner prompt: List at least two things that worked well and at least two things that didn't go as planned during the capstone week, across any of your systems.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reflection, risks, and backup plans complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Write the full content of your presentation: one thing that worked, one thing that didn't, and one specific backup plan for a risk that could recur.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My presentation names one specific thing that worked during the capstone week and why it worked.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My presentation names one specific thing that did not go as planned during the capstone week.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My presentation includes one specific backup plan for a risk that could recur, naming the exact trigger and the exact different action I would take.

Equal-access rule: If presenting out loud is not possible, the learner instead writes the complete presentation as a script, covering the same three parts (what worked, what didn't, and the backup plan), and a trusted adult reads the full script and initials it to confirm they read and understood it.

resources.title: reflection, risks, and backup plans minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Of the five systems (planning, household, food, transportation, communication), which one do you most want to strengthen going forward, and what is your first specific step?

Success checks: Presentation content and specificity: Presentation names one specific thing that worked, one specific thing that didn't, and one specific backup plan naming the trigger and the different action. | Guardian-confirmed presentation and engagement: Guardian confirms the presentation happened, live or via the initialed script, and confirms asking at least one follow-up question.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reflection, risks, and backup plans supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reflection, risks, and backup plans condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Presentation content and specificity: Presentation names one specific thing that worked, one specific thing that didn't, and one specific backup plan naming the trigger and the different action. | Guardian-confirmed presentation and engagement: Guardian confirms the presentation happened, live or via the initialed script, and confirms asking at least one follow-up question..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Presentation content and specificity: Presentation names one specific thing that worked, one specific thing that didn't, and one specific backup plan naming the trigger and the different action. | Guardian-confirmed presentation and engagement: Guardian confirms the presentation happened, live or via the initialed script, and confirms asking at least one follow-up question.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
